    59	@op
    60	def project_out(w: np.ndarray, direction: np.ndarray, axis: int = 0,
    61	                index: list[int] | None = None) -> np.ndarray:
    62	    """Remove the component along a unit ``direction`` from selected rows/columns.
    63	
    64	    ``axis=0``: each selected row ``w[i, :]`` loses its projection onto the
    65	    direction (direction has length ``w.shape[1]``). ``axis=1``: each selected
    66	    column ``w[:, j]`` does (direction has length ``w.shape[0]``). This is the
    67	    Exp-8 edit of the post — subtract one direction from N output columns.
    68	    """
    69	    d = np.asarray(direction, dtype=np.float64)
    70	    nrm = np.linalg.norm(d)
    71	    if nrm == 0:
    72	        raise ValueError("direction has zero norm")
    73	    d = d / nrm
    74	    out = w.astype(np.float64).copy()
    75	    if axis == 0:
    76	        if d.shape[0] != w.shape[1]:
    77	            raise ValueError("direction length must equal the number of columns")
    78	        rows = np.arange(w.shape[0]) if index is None else np.asarray(index)
    79	        out[rows] -= np.outer(out[rows] @ d, d)
    80	    elif axis == 1:
    81	        if d.shape[0] != w.shape[0]:
    82	            raise ValueError("direction length must equal the number of rows")
    83	        cols = np.arange(w.shape[1]) if index is None else np.asarray(index)
    84	        out[:, cols] -= np.outer(d, d @ out[:, cols])
    85	    else:
    86	        raise ValueError("axis must be 0 or 1")
    87	    return out.astype(w.dtype)

    93

    95	    row (index 127) ever sees data; the other 254 see zero padding and carry
    96	    gradient-free weights. Keeping that row is function-preserving once the
    97	    layer's padding is set to 0 in the VGSL spec (``Cr1,1,85,1,1``).
    98	    """
    99	    return np.take(w, [keep], axis=axis).copy()
